# o2pg rule reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_rules_doc.py from the rule registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

97 rules. Effort is in effort points per affected object. Rules marked **AI risk** feed the AI readiness section of the report.

| Category | Prefix | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| datatypes | DT | 17 |
| plsql | PL | 18 |

## datatypes

### O2PG-DT-001: NUMBER without declared precision

severity **medium** · effort 0.1 · **AI risk**

Bare NUMBER (and INTEGER, which Oracle stores as NUMBER(*,0)) accepts up to 38 significant digits. There is no single right PostgreSQL type without knowing the data.

**Remediation:** Map to numeric to stay safe. Profile MAX/MIN and scale per column, then narrow to integer, bigint or numeric(p,s) where the data allows. Keys joined to other tables should end up with the same type on both sides.

**Tell the model:** Bare NUMBER is not an integer and not a float. Tell the model to map it to numeric unless you give it a profiled precision and scale.

### O2PG-DT-002: Binary and approximate numeric types

severity **low** · effort 0.1

FLOAT in Oracle is a decimal type with binary precision; BINARY_FLOAT and BINARY_DOUBLE are IEEE types with their own NaN and infinity literals.

**Remediation:** BINARY_FLOAT -> real, BINARY_DOUBLE -> double precision. For FLOAT use numeric when values must round-trip exactly, otherwise double precision. Replace BINARY_FLOAT_NAN style literals with 'NaN'::float8.

### O2PG-DT-003: DATE columns carry a time of day

severity **high** · effort 0.25 · **AI risk**

Oracle DATE stores year to second. PostgreSQL date has no time at all, so a name-for-name mapping silently drops the time portion.

**Remediation:** Map to timestamp(0). Only use date after checking that every row has a midnight time (e.g. COUNT(*) WHERE col <> TRUNC(col) = 0). Review TRUNC(col) and col + n arithmetic in code at the same time.

**Tell the model:** Oracle DATE includes hours, minutes and seconds. Tell the model to map DATE to timestamp(0), not date.

### O2PG-DT-004: Time zone aware timestamps

severity **medium** · effort 0.25

TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE keeps the original offset or region in Oracle. TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE converts to the session zone. PostgreSQL timestamptz stores UTC and renders in the session TimeZone, so the original zone is lost.

**Remediation:** Map both to timestamptz. If the original zone matters, add a separate text column holding the IANA zone name. Set the server TimeZone parameter on Azure explicitly rather than relying on the default (UTC).

### O2PG-DT-005: Character columns with BYTE length semantics

severity **low** · effort 0.05 · **AI risk**

VARCHAR2(n BYTE) limits bytes, not characters. PostgreSQL varchar(n) limits characters, so the limit effectively grows for multibyte data.

**Remediation:** Usually harmless for the database, but application-side validation that mirrors the byte limit may now disagree with the column. Decide on character limits explicitly.

**Tell the model:** VARCHAR2 lengths here are in bytes. Tell the model whether you want character lengths kept as-is or recalculated.

### O2PG-DT-006: NOT NULL character columns will start accepting empty strings

severity **medium** · effort 0.1 · **AI risk**

Oracle treats '' as NULL, so NOT NULL on a VARCHAR2 also rejects empty strings. In PostgreSQL '' is a real value and passes NOT NULL. The constraint gets weaker after migration without anyone touching it.

**Remediation:** Where the business rule is 'must have a value', add CHECK (col <> '') or CHECK (btrim(col) <> '') next to NOT NULL.

**Tell the model:** In Oracle '' IS NULL. Tell the model that NOT NULL character columns must also reject empty strings, and to add CHECK (col <> '') where that matters.

### O2PG-DT-007: CHAR columns and blank padding

severity **low** · effort 0.1

CHAR(n) pads with blanks in both databases, but comparison and concatenation rules differ. In PostgreSQL trailing blanks of character(n) are insignificant and are dropped when cast to text, which changes LENGTH() and || results.

**Remediation:** Prefer varchar(n) or text unless the fixed width is genuinely required. If you keep char(n), test any code that compares CHAR with VARCHAR2 values or relies on padding.

### O2PG-DT-008: LONG and LONG RAW columns

severity **high** · effort 1

LONG types have been deprecated for decades and carry many restrictions. Migration tools often need special handling to extract them, and code that reads them piecewise must change.

**Remediation:** LONG -> text, LONG RAW -> bytea. Check that your data movement tool supports LONG extraction and test with the largest values.

### O2PG-DT-009: LOB columns

severity **medium** · effort 0.5

CLOB and BLOB map to text and bytea, which are limited to 1 GB per value and are read in one piece. DBMS_LOB code and locator-based APIs do not carry over.

**Remediation:** Map CLOB/NCLOB -> text and BLOB -> bytea. Check the largest value per column. For very large binaries consider Azure Blob Storage with a URL column instead of storing bytes in the database. Data loads of LOB-heavy tables are usually the slowest part.

### O2PG-DT-010: BFILE columns

severity **blocker** · effort 3

BFILE points at a file on the database server's file system. Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server gives you no file system access, so there is nothing to point at.

**Remediation:** Move the files to Azure Blob Storage and store the blob URL or path in a text column. File reads move to the application.

### O2PG-DT-011: XMLTYPE columns

severity **medium** · effort 1

PostgreSQL has an xml type with xpath() and XMLTABLE, but no XQuery, no XML indexes and no XML schema validation. Storage options (binary XML, object-relational) do not carry over.

**Remediation:** Map to xml if you query it with XPath, or to jsonb if you control the format and mostly query it. Rewrite EXTRACT/EXTRACTVALUE/XMLQUERY calls.

### O2PG-DT-012: SDO_GEOMETRY (Oracle Spatial) columns

severity **high** · effort 2 · extensions: `postgis`

Oracle Spatial geometries need PostGIS. SRIDs, spatial indexes and SDO_* functions all need translation.

**Remediation:** Allow-list postgis in azure.extensions, CREATE EXTENSION postgis, map to geometry(<type>, <srid>), replace spatial indexes with GiST, and rewrite SDO_RELATE / SDO_WITHIN_DISTANCE as ST_Intersects / ST_DWithin.

### O2PG-DT-013: ROWID and UROWID columns

severity **medium** · effort 0.5

Stored ROWIDs are physical addresses into Oracle. PostgreSQL's ctid changes on every update and VACUUM FULL, so it cannot replace them.

**Remediation:** Find what the stored ROWID points at and replace it with that row's primary key.

### O2PG-DT-014: Virtual columns

severity **low** · effort 0.25

PostgreSQL generated columns are computed on write and stored. The expression must use immutable functions only, which rules out SYSDATE and most NLS-dependent calls.

**Remediation:** Use GENERATED ALWAYS AS (expr) STORED and translate the expression. If it is not immutable, use a view or a trigger instead.

### O2PG-DT-015: Column defaults that use Oracle functions

severity **low** · effort 0.1

Defaults such as SYSDATE, SYS_GUID(), USER or seq.NEXTVAL do not exist in PostgreSQL.

**Remediation:** SYSDATE -> LOCALTIMESTAMP(0) or clock_timestamp() (see the SYSDATE rule for the difference), SYS_GUID() -> gen_random_uuid(), USER -> current_user, seq.NEXTVAL -> nextval('seq') or an identity column.

### O2PG-DT-016: Columns of user-defined object or collection types

severity **high** · effort 1.5

Columns typed as Oracle object types, VARRAYs or nested tables. PostgreSQL has composite types and arrays, but no methods, no nested table storage and different constructor syntax.

**Remediation:** Usually the cleanest answer is to normalise: nested tables and VARRAYs become child tables, object types become plain columns. Arrays or jsonb are reasonable when the data is only ever read as a whole.

### O2PG-DT-017: Data types with no automatic mapping

severity **high** · effort 1

Oracle-supplied types o2pg does not know how to map (ANYDATA, URITYPE, ORDImage, media types and so on).

**Remediation:** Decide per column: jsonb for self-describing payloads, text for URIs, Blob Storage for media. Check whether the column is still used before investing in it.

## plsql

### O2PG-PL-001: Packages

severity **medium** · effort 2

PostgreSQL has no packages. Specs, bodies, private subprograms and package-level types all need a new home.

**Remediation:** The usual pattern is one schema per package with one function or procedure per subprogram. Private subprograms become functions you do not grant EXECUTE on. Package types become composite types in that schema. The orafce extension does not emulate packages.

### O2PG-PL-002: Package-level state (global variables)

severity **high** · effort 3 · **AI risk**

Variables declared at package level keep their value for the whole session. Code often relies on that as a cache or as a way to pass context between calls. PostgreSQL functions have no persistent state.

**Remediation:** Replace with session settings (set_config / current_setting with a custom prefix), temporary tables, or pass the value explicitly. Read-only lookups usually become a table or an IMMUTABLE function.

**Tell the model:** These packages keep state between calls. A model converting one function at a time cannot see that; tell it which variables are session state and how you want them replaced (for example current_setting('app.x')).

### O2PG-PL-003: Autonomous transactions

severity **high** · effort 3 · **AI risk** · extensions: `postgres_fdw`

PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION commits independently of the caller. It is most often used for error logging that must survive a rollback. PostgreSQL has no equivalent.

**Remediation:** Options: write the log through a separate connection (postgres_fdw to the same server is a known workaround), move logging to the application, or use RAISE LOG and Azure Monitor / server logs. Re-check the business rule before emulating it.

**Tell the model:** Autonomous transactions commit even when the caller rolls back. Models tend to drop the pragma and silently change that behaviour; tell it how you want it handled.

### O2PG-PL-004: BULK COLLECT and FORALL

severity **low** · effort 0.5

Bulk binding exists to cut context switches between PL/SQL and SQL. PL/pgSQL has no BULK COLLECT or FORALL syntax.

**Remediation:** Usually the best rewrite is a single set-based INSERT ... SELECT or UPDATE ... FROM. Otherwise use arrays (array_agg, unnest) or a plain FOR loop over a query.

### O2PG-PL-005: REF CURSOR and SYS_REFCURSOR

severity **medium** · effort 1

PostgreSQL has refcursor, but the client side differs: cursors are only valid inside a transaction and drivers fetch them differently.

**Remediation:** Map to refcursor, or better, to RETURNS TABLE / RETURNS SETOF functions. Check the application data access layer, which is usually where the real work is.

### O2PG-PL-006: %TYPE and %ROWTYPE anchored declarations

severity **info** · effort 0

PL/pgSQL supports %TYPE and %ROWTYPE, so these mostly convert as-is.

**Remediation:** No change needed in most cases. Make sure the anchored table or column exists with the same name in PostgreSQL (watch for case folding).

### O2PG-PL-007: Dynamic SQL (EXECUTE IMMEDIATE, DBMS_SQL)

severity **medium** · effort 1.5 · **AI risk**

SQL built in strings is invisible to static analysis, including this tool. Statements inside the strings are Oracle dialect too.

**Remediation:** EXECUTE IMMEDIATE -> EXECUTE ... USING; DBMS_SQL -> EXECUTE with format() and %I/%L. Review every string by hand for Oracle syntax and SQL injection.

**Tell the model:** SQL inside strings is not visible as SQL. Tell the model to convert the dialect inside dynamic SQL strings as well, and review those strings yourself.

### O2PG-PL-008: DBMS_LOB usage

severity **medium** · effort 1

PostgreSQL text and bytea are values, not locators. DBMS_LOB has no equivalent.

**Remediation:** Replace DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR/INSTR/GETLENGTH/APPEND with substr, strpos, length and ||. Code that streams large LOBs in chunks may be better moved to the application.

### O2PG-PL-009: UTL_FILE file access

severity **blocker** · effort 4

Reading and writing server files is not possible on Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server; there is no file system you can reach from SQL.

**Remediation:** Move file import/export to the application, Azure Data Factory or an Azure Function writing to Blob Storage. For bulk loads use COPY FROM STDIN from a client.

### O2PG-PL-010: Network calls from the database (UTL_HTTP, UTL_SMTP, UTL_TCP, UTL_MAIL)

severity **blocker** · effort 4

The database calling web services or sending mail has no supported equivalent on Flexible Server.

**Remediation:** Write an outbox table inside the transaction and have an application worker, Azure Function or Logic App deliver the message. This is usually more reliable anyway.

### O2PG-PL-011: Job scheduling from code (DBMS_JOB, DBMS_SCHEDULER)

severity **medium** · effort 1 · extensions: `pg_cron`

Code that creates or runs scheduler jobs at runtime.

**Remediation:** Use pg_cron (cron.schedule / cron.unschedule). On Azure, add pg_cron to shared_preload_libraries and azure.extensions; jobs are created from the database named in cron.database_name (postgres by default) and can target others with cron.schedule_in_database.

### O2PG-PL-012: Other Oracle-supplied packages (DBMS_*, UTL_*)

severity **medium** · effort 0.75 · extensions: `pgcrypto`, `orafce`

Calls to Oracle-supplied packages that do not have a dedicated rule. Each needs a replacement built-in, extension or rewrite.

**Remediation:** See the per-object detail for a suggested replacement. Common ones: DBMS_OUTPUT -> RAISE NOTICE, DBMS_CRYPTO -> pgcrypto, DBMS_LOCK.SLEEP -> pg_sleep, DBMS_ALERT and DBMS_PIPE -> LISTEN/NOTIFY. orafce provides DBMS_OUTPUT and UTL_FILE-style functions, but its UTL_FILE needs server directories that Azure does not expose.

### O2PG-PL-013: RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR and Oracle error codes

severity **low** · effort 0.5 · **AI risk**

Applications often match on ORA-20xxx numbers or SQLCODE values. PostgreSQL uses five-character SQLSTATE codes.

**Remediation:** RAISE EXCEPTION '...' USING ERRCODE = 'P0001' (or a custom 5-character code), and update application error handling that parses ORA- numbers.

**Tell the model:** Error numbers are part of the contract with the application. Give the model a mapping from ORA-20xxx codes to SQLSTATE values instead of letting it invent one.

### O2PG-PL-014: Transaction control inside stored code

severity **medium** · effort 1

PostgreSQL functions cannot COMMIT or ROLLBACK. Procedures can (PostgreSQL 11+), but only when called with CALL outside an explicit transaction block.

**Remediation:** Convert units that commit into procedures, or move the commit to the caller. Savepoint-style ROLLBACK TO becomes a BEGIN ... EXCEPTION block.

### O2PG-PL-015: Wrapped (obfuscated) PL/SQL

severity **blocker** · effort 5

The source was created with the wrap utility, so nobody can read or convert it.

**Remediation:** Get the original source from version control or the vendor. Without it the unit has to be rewritten from its observed behaviour.

### O2PG-PL-016: Pipelined table functions

severity **medium** · effort 1

PIPELINED functions stream rows to a SELECT ... FROM TABLE(f()) caller.

**Remediation:** Rewrite as RETURNS SETOF / RETURNS TABLE with RETURN NEXT or RETURN QUERY, and drop the TABLE() wrapper at call sites.

### O2PG-PL-017: GOTO statements

severity **low** · effort 1

PL/pgSQL has no GOTO statement, so jumps to labels must be restructured.

**Remediation:** Restructure with loops, EXIT/CONTINUE with labels, or early RETURN.

### O2PG-PL-018: Associative arrays (INDEX BY tables)

severity **medium** · effort 1 · extensions: `hstore`

Associative arrays are sparse maps keyed by integer or string. PostgreSQL arrays are dense and 1-based.

**Remediation:** Integer-keyed dense arrays -> PostgreSQL arrays. String-keyed maps -> jsonb or hstore. Often a temporary table or a join removes the need entirely.

## sql-dialect

### O2PG-SQ-001: Hierarchical queries (CONNECT BY)

severity **high** · effort 2

CONNECT BY, START WITH, PRIOR, LEVEL, SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH and ORDER SIBLINGS BY have no direct PostgreSQL syntax.

**Remediation:** Rewrite as WITH RECURSIVE. Carry a depth column for LEVEL, build a path array for SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH and ORDER SIBLINGS BY, and add a CYCLE clause (PostgreSQL 14+) where NOCYCLE was used.

### O2PG-SQ-002: ROWNUM

severity **medium** · effort 0.75 · **AI risk**

ROWNUM is assigned before ORDER BY is applied. 'WHERE ROWNUM <= 10 ORDER BY x' returns 10 arbitrary rows, sorted, not the top 10.

**Remediation:** Use LIMIT / FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY for top-n, and row_number() OVER (...) where ROWNUM is used as a value. Decide whether the original ordering bug is a feature.

**Tell the model:** ROWNUM filters before ORDER BY. A model will usually 'fix' this into a correct top-n with LIMIT, which changes results. Tell it whether to keep the old behaviour.

### O2PG-SQ-003: DECODE

severity **low** · effort 0.25 · extensions: `orafce`

DECODE is Oracle-only. It also treats NULL = NULL as a match, unlike CASE.

**Remediation:** Rewrite as CASE. Where DECODE compared NULLs, use IS NOT DISTINCT FROM in the CASE. orafce ships a decode() function for common type combinations if you need a bridge.

### O2PG-SQ-004: NVL and NVL2

severity **low** · effort 0.1 · extensions: `orafce`

NVL and NVL2 are Oracle functions. NVL evaluates both arguments; COALESCE short-circuits.

**Remediation:** NVL(a,b) -> COALESCE(a,b); NVL2(a,b,c) -> CASE WHEN a IS NOT NULL THEN b ELSE c END. orafce provides nvl and nvl2.

### O2PG-SQ-005: Oracle outer join operator (+)

severity **medium** · effort 0.75

The (+) operator is not supported. Conditions in WHERE must move into ON clauses.

**Remediation:** Rewrite as ANSI LEFT/RIGHT JOIN. Be careful with filters on the outer table: in Oracle they carried (+) too, and they must go into the ON clause, not WHERE.

### O2PG-SQ-006: MERGE statements

severity **medium** · effort 1

PostgreSQL 15+ supports MERGE, but not Oracle's DELETE WHERE inside WHEN MATCHED, and concurrency behaviour differs from INSERT ... ON CONFLICT.

**Remediation:** On Azure Flexible Server pick PostgreSQL 15 or later and use MERGE, or use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE for single-row upserts that must be safe under concurrency.

### O2PG-SQ-007: SYSDATE and SYSTIMESTAMP

severity **medium** · effort 0.25 · **AI risk**

SYSDATE returns the database server's OS clock, ignores the session time zone and advances during a transaction. now() / CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is frozen at transaction start and is time zone aware.

**Remediation:** LOCALTIMESTAMP(0) is the closest match for SYSDATE inside one statement; use clock_timestamp() where the value must move during a long transaction. Azure servers run in UTC unless you change the TimeZone parameter.

**Tell the model:** SYSDATE is server local time and changes within a transaction. Tell the model which PostgreSQL function you want (LOCALTIMESTAMP, now() or clock_timestamp()).

### O2PG-SQ-008: Empty string literals ('' is NULL in Oracle)

severity **high** · effort 1 · **AI risk**

In Oracle '' is NULL, so col = '' is never true, NVL(col, '') does nothing and assigning '' stores NULL. In PostgreSQL all of these behave differently.

**Remediation:** Review each use. Comparisons with '' usually become IS NULL, or COALESCE(col, '') = '' if both should count as empty. Decide on one convention for the data load too (convert '' to NULL, or the reverse).

**Tell the model:** Oracle treats '' as NULL everywhere. A model will translate '' literally. Tell it to treat every '' as NULL and to flag comparisons with '' for review.

### O2PG-SQ-009: SELECT ... FROM DUAL

severity **low** · effort 0.1 · extensions: `orafce`

PostgreSQL does not need or have DUAL.

**Remediation:** Drop FROM DUAL; in PL/pgSQL assign directly (v := expr). orafce creates a dual table if you need a bridge.

### O2PG-SQ-010: MINUS set operator

severity **low** · effort 0.1

MINUS is spelled EXCEPT in PostgreSQL.

**Remediation:** Replace MINUS with EXCEPT (EXCEPT ALL if duplicates matter).

### O2PG-SQ-011: Oracle date functions

severity **low** · effort 0.25 · extensions: `orafce`

ADD_MONTHS, MONTHS_BETWEEN, LAST_DAY, NEXT_DAY and TRUNC(date) are Oracle built-ins.

**Remediation:** Use interval arithmetic and date_trunc(), or enable orafce, which provides add_months, months_between, last_day and next_day with Oracle semantics.

### O2PG-SQ-012: TO_DATE / TO_CHAR / TO_NUMBER format models

severity **medium** · effort 0.25 · **AI risk**

PostgreSQL has these functions, but format models differ in the details (RR, FM, D, J, NLS parameters), PostgreSQL to_date is more lenient, and calls without a format rely on Oracle's NLS_DATE_FORMAT.

**Remediation:** Check every format model, and add an explicit one wherever the Oracle code relied on NLS defaults. Test with boundary dates and invalid input.

**Tell the model:** Conversions without an explicit format depend on NLS session settings the model cannot see. Give it the NLS_DATE_FORMAT and NLS_NUMERIC_CHARACTERS in use.

### O2PG-SQ-013: Optimizer hints

severity **low** · effort 0.1 · extensions: `pg_stat_statements`

Hints become ordinary comments in PostgreSQL. Anything that only performs well because of a hint may need a different index or a rewrite.

**Remediation:** Note which statements were hinted and why, and include them in performance tests. Use pg_stat_statements on Azure to find the slow ones after cutover.

### O2PG-SQ-014: Sequence NEXTVAL / CURRVAL

severity **low** · effort 0.1

seq.NEXTVAL is Oracle syntax. CURRVAL semantics are per session in both databases.

**Remediation:** seq.NEXTVAL -> nextval('seq'), seq.CURRVAL -> currval('seq'). Consider identity columns.

### O2PG-SQ-015: USER, USERENV and SYS_CONTEXT

severity **medium** · effort 0.5

Session context functions. SYS_CONTEXT is also how Oracle VPD and application contexts pass values around.

**Remediation:** USER -> current_user (or session_user). SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV', ...) -> inet_client_addr(), current_database(), current_setting(...). Custom application contexts -> set_config('app.x', ...) / current_setting('app.x', true).

### O2PG-SQ-016: Flashback queries

severity **high** · effort 2

AS OF TIMESTAMP / SCN and VERSIONS BETWEEN read old row versions. PostgreSQL cannot.

**Remediation:** If the code needs history, add history tables maintained by triggers or the application. For recovery, Azure Flexible Server point-in-time restore replaces the operational use of flashback.

### O2PG-SQ-017: Date arithmetic with numbers

severity **medium** · effort 0.25 · **AI risk**

In Oracle DATE + 1 adds a day and DATE + 1/24 adds an hour. Once DATE becomes timestamp, timestamp + integer is an error in PostgreSQL.

**Remediation:** Use intervals: col + interval '1 day', col + make_interval(hours => n).

**Tell the model:** Numbers added to dates are days (fractions are hours and minutes). Tell the model to convert them to intervals after DATE becomes timestamp(0).

### O2PG-SQ-018: String concatenation with possible NULLs

severity **medium** · effort 0.25 · **AI risk**

In Oracle 'a' || NULL is 'a'. In PostgreSQL it is NULL. Any concatenation that can see a NULL column changes result.

**Remediation:** Use concat() or concat_ws(), which ignore NULLs, or wrap nullable operands in COALESCE(x, '').

**Tell the model:** Oracle || ignores NULLs; PostgreSQL || returns NULL. Tell the model to use concat() or COALESCE for any nullable operand.

## objects

### O2PG-OB-001: Private synonyms

severity **low** · effort 0.25

PostgreSQL has no synonyms. Code that relies on them resolves names differently.

**Remediation:** Most private synonyms just point at another schema: set search_path for the role (ALTER ROLE app SET search_path = app, hr) or qualify names. For renames, use a view, or a wrapper function for synonyms that point at code.

### O2PG-OB-002: Public synonyms

severity **medium** · effort 0.5

Public synonyms make an object visible to every user without a schema prefix. There is no global namespace like that in PostgreSQL.

**Remediation:** Add the owning schema to search_path for the roles that use the objects (ALTER ROLE ... SET search_path, or ALTER DATABASE ... SET search_path).

### O2PG-OB-003: Database links

severity **high** · effort 3 · extensions: `postgres_fdw`

Database links (and synonyms that reach through them) let SQL query another database. On Azure Flexible Server postgres_fdw can reach other PostgreSQL servers, but there is no supported way to query a remaining Oracle database from the PostgreSQL side.

**Remediation:** Links to databases that also move to PostgreSQL -> postgres_fdw with a foreign server and user mapping (check outbound networking from the server's VNet or firewall). Links to systems that stay on Oracle -> move the integration into the application or a data pipeline, and plan the cutover order around it. Credentials stored in links become user mappings; rotate them.

### O2PG-OB-004: Row-level DML triggers

severity **medium** · effort 1 · **AI risk**

Row triggers carry business logic that does not show up in table DDL: audit columns, derived values, cascades into other tables. PostgreSQL triggers call a separate trigger function and use NEW/OLD instead of :NEW/:OLD.

**Remediation:** Create a trigger function (RETURNS trigger) per trigger and a CREATE TRIGGER that calls it. Replace :NEW/:OLD with NEW/OLD, INSERTING/UPDATING/DELETING with TG_OP, and remember BEFORE row triggers must RETURN NEW. Sequence-filling triggers can usually be replaced by identity columns.

**Tell the model:** Triggers change data the DDL does not mention. Give the model the trigger bodies along with the table, or it will produce tables that silently lose those side effects.

### O2PG-OB-005: Compound triggers

severity **high** · effort 2

Compound triggers combine statement and row timing points with shared state, usually to work around mutating-table errors.

**Remediation:** Split into separate row and statement triggers. In PostgreSQL 10+ AFTER statement triggers with transition tables (REFERENCING NEW TABLE AS ...) often replace the whole pattern, since PostgreSQL has no mutating-table restriction.

### O2PG-OB-006: Schema and database event triggers

severity **high** · effort 2

DDL, logon and startup triggers defined on SCHEMA or DATABASE. PostgreSQL event triggers cover DDL only; there is no logon trigger.

**Remediation:** DDL auditing -> event triggers or Azure server logs. Logon logic -> role settings (ALTER ROLE ... SET), connection pool init SQL or the application.

### O2PG-OB-007: Sequences with MAXVALUE beyond bigint

severity **low** · effort 0.1

Oracle's default sequence MAXVALUE is 10^28 - 1. PostgreSQL sequences are bigint, so CREATE SEQUENCE fails if the value is copied as-is.

**Remediation:** Drop MAXVALUE (defaults to bigint max) or cap it at 9223372036854775807.

### O2PG-OB-008: Sequences must be re-synced after the data load

severity **info** · effort 0.05

Loading data does not move sequences. After cutover each sequence must start above the highest value already used, or inserts start failing with duplicates.

**Remediation:** After the final load run setval('seq', (SELECT max(id) FROM t)) per sequence, or use the Oracle LAST_NUMBER captured at cutover plus a safety margin.

### O2PG-OB-009: Materialized views refreshed ON COMMIT

severity **high** · effort 3

PostgreSQL materialized views are only refreshed by an explicit REFRESH, which is always a full rebuild. Nothing keeps them in sync on commit.

**Remediation:** Replace with a plain table maintained by triggers on the base tables, or accept staleness and refresh on a schedule. If the view exists only for query rewrite, a normal view plus indexes may be enough.

### O2PG-OB-010: Materialized views with fast (incremental) refresh

severity **medium** · effort 1.5 · extensions: `pg_cron`

Fast refresh relies on materialized view logs. PostgreSQL has no incremental refresh; REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY still recomputes everything, it just avoids blocking readers.

**Remediation:** Schedule REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY (needs a unique index) with pg_cron and check that the refresh time fits the window, or maintain a summary table incrementally with triggers.

### O2PG-OB-011: Global temporary tables

severity **medium** · effort 1

Oracle GTTs are permanent definitions with per-session data. PostgreSQL temporary tables are created per session, so code that expects the table to already exist breaks.

**Remediation:** Create the temp table at the start of the session or procedure (CREATE TEMP TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ... ON COMMIT DELETE ROWS), or use an unlogged table keyed by session/transaction id. Watch catalog bloat if temp tables are created very often.

### O2PG-OB-012: User-defined object and collection types

severity **high** · effort 1.5

Object types, VARRAYs and nested table types. PostgreSQL composite types have no methods, inheritance or constructors with defaults.

**Remediation:** Object types used only in PL/SQL -> composite types. Member methods -> plain functions taking the composite as the first argument. Collections -> arrays. Types used as column types: see O2PG-DT-016.

### O2PG-OB-013: Invalid objects

severity **medium** · effort 0.25

Objects that do not compile in Oracle today. Converting them costs time and they may be dead code.

**Remediation:** Recompile in Oracle (UTL_RECOMP or ALTER ... COMPILE). Anything that still fails and is not referenced should be dropped from scope, not migrated.

### O2PG-OB-014: Tables without a primary key

severity **medium** · effort 0.5

Logical replication, most change data capture tools and row-by-row validation all need a key. Without one, online migration and data comparison get much harder.

**Remediation:** Add a primary key where a natural or surrogate key exists. Otherwise set REPLICA IDENTITY FULL on the PostgreSQL side for replication, and expect slower apply.

### O2PG-OB-015: Identifiers longer than 63 bytes

severity **high** · effort 0.5

Oracle 12.2+ allows 128-byte names. PostgreSQL truncates identifiers to 63 bytes, so two long names with the same prefix collide, and generated DDL can fail.

**Remediation:** Rename before conversion and keep a rename map so code and the application can be updated consistently.

### O2PG-OB-016: Quoted, mixed-case or special-character identifiers

severity **medium** · effort 0.25 · **AI risk**

Oracle folds unquoted names to upper case; PostgreSQL folds them to lower case. Names created with quotes in mixed case or with characters such as # or spaces will need quotes forever in PostgreSQL.

**Remediation:** Convert to lower-case snake_case names during migration and keep a rename map. Do not carry the quotes over unless the application cannot change.

**Tell the model:** Upper-case Oracle names copied with quotes ("EMPLOYEES") force quoting in every PostgreSQL query. Tell the model to emit unquoted lower-case names and list the identifiers that really are case-sensitive.

### O2PG-OB-017: Names that are reserved words in PostgreSQL

severity **medium** · effort 0.25

Some names that are legal unquoted in Oracle (LIMIT, OFFSET, ANALYZE, WINDOW, RETURNING, ...) are reserved in PostgreSQL and fail in DDL and queries unless quoted.

**Remediation:** Rename the table or column (for example limit -> credit_limit), or quote it everywhere.

## partitioning

### O2PG-PT-001: Range, list and hash partitioned tables

severity **low** · effort 1 · extensions: `pg_partman`

PostgreSQL declarative partitioning supports RANGE, LIST and HASH. The syntax is different and each partition is created as its own table.

**Remediation:** CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION BY RANGE (key) and one CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF per partition. Add a DEFAULT partition where Oracle used MAXVALUE or DEFAULT. pg_partman automates creating and dropping time-based partitions.

### O2PG-PT-002: Interval partitioning

severity **medium** · effort 1.5 · extensions: `pg_partman`, `pg_cron`

Oracle creates interval partitions automatically on insert. PostgreSQL never creates partitions on its own; rows with no matching partition fail or land in DEFAULT.

**Remediation:** Use pg_partman with a premake count and run its maintenance from pg_cron (both are available on Azure Flexible Server). Keep a DEFAULT partition and alert if it ever receives rows.

### O2PG-PT-003: Reference and system partitioning

severity **high** · effort 3

REFERENCE partitioning inherits the parent's scheme through a foreign key; SYSTEM partitioning lets the application pick the partition. Neither exists in PostgreSQL.

**Remediation:** For reference partitioning, copy the parent's partition key into the child table, partition the child on it and include it in the foreign key. System partitioning usually becomes HASH or LIST partitioning on an explicit column.

### O2PG-PT-004: Composite (sub)partitioning

severity **medium** · effort 1.5

Sub-partitions become partitions of partitions in PostgreSQL. Every level is a real table, so the object count grows quickly.

**Remediation:** Create each partition with its own PARTITION BY clause. Check that the total number of leaf partitions stays reasonable (planning time grows with it), and consider dropping the second level if it existed only for storage management.

### O2PG-PT-005: Primary or unique keys that do not include the partition key

severity **high** · effort 1.5

PostgreSQL requires every primary key and unique constraint on a partitioned table to include all partition key columns. Oracle does not (it uses global indexes), so these constraints cannot be created as-is.

**Remediation:** Either add the partition key to the constraint (which weakens uniqueness to 'unique per partition key value'), enforce global uniqueness another way, or change the partition key. Decide this before moving data.

### O2PG-PT-006: Global indexes on partitioned tables

severity **medium** · effort 0.5

A non-partitioned index on a partitioned table is a global index. PostgreSQL only has local (per-partition) indexes.

**Remediation:** Recreate as a regular index on the parent, which PostgreSQL builds on every partition. Queries that relied on a global index without the partition key in the WHERE clause will scan every partition's index; test them.

## security

### O2PG-SE-001: Virtual Private Database (VPD) policies

severity **high** · effort 3

VPD policies add predicates to queries through a policy function. PostgreSQL row level security is the equivalent, but policies are SQL expressions on the table, not functions returning predicate strings.

**Remediation:** ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and CREATE POLICY ... USING (...) per policy. Move the context values the policy function read from SYS_CONTEXT into current_setting('app.x'). Remember table owners bypass RLS unless FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is set.

### O2PG-SE-002: TDE column encryption

severity **medium** · effort 0.5 · extensions: `pgcrypto`

Transparent Data Encryption at column level. Azure Database for PostgreSQL encrypts all storage at rest by default (optionally with customer-managed keys in Key Vault), but has no transparent per-column encryption.

**Remediation:** If at-rest encryption was the requirement, Azure storage encryption covers it. If the column must stay unreadable to DBAs, encrypt in the application or use pgcrypto with keys held outside the database.

### O2PG-SE-003: Object privileges granted to PUBLIC

severity **medium** · effort 0.25

Grants to PUBLIC are visible to every role. Carrying them over keeps an open door you may not have intended.

**Remediation:** Replace with grants to an explicit role. Also REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC on older PostgreSQL versions (15+ does this by default).

### O2PG-SE-004: Definer-rights program units

severity **medium** · effort 0.25 · **AI risk**

Oracle program units run with the owner's privileges unless declared AUTHID CURRENT_USER. PostgreSQL functions default to SECURITY INVOKER, the opposite.

**Remediation:** Decide per unit. Where definer rights are really needed, use SECURITY DEFINER and always pin search_path (SET search_path = schema, pg_temp) to avoid hijacking. Elsewhere, grant the caller the privileges it needs.

**Tell the model:** Oracle code runs as its owner by default; PostgreSQL code runs as the caller. Tell the model which units need SECURITY DEFINER, or permissions will break.

### O2PG-SE-005: Fine-grained auditing, redaction and RLS APIs

severity **medium** · effort 1

Code that manages auditing policies (DBMS_FGA), data redaction (DBMS_REDACT) or VPD policies (DBMS_RLS) at runtime.

**Remediation:** DBMS_RLS -> CREATE POLICY. DBMS_REDACT -> views or column privileges that mask data. DBMS_FGA -> statement logging; check whether pgaudit is available for your server version before planning around it.

### O2PG-SE-006: Object privileges to map to roles

severity **info** · effort 0.1

Summary of who holds object privileges on the analysed schemas. Each grantee becomes a role (or a member of one) in PostgreSQL.

**Remediation:** Create group roles (NOLOGIN) for each grantee pattern, grant privileges to the group, and use ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES so new objects inherit them.

## performance

### O2PG-PF-001: Bitmap indexes

severity **medium** · effort 0.5

PostgreSQL has no stored bitmap indexes. It builds bitmaps at query time from ordinary B-tree indexes and combines them, which covers most of the same queries.

**Remediation:** Create B-tree indexes on the same columns, or a partial index for the selective values. For very large append-only tables BRIN is worth testing. Verify the star queries that relied on bitmap AND/OR.

### O2PG-PF-002: Function-based indexes

severity **low** · effort 0.25

PostgreSQL expression indexes are the equivalent, but every function in the expression must be IMMUTABLE and the query must use the same expression.

**Remediation:** CREATE INDEX ... ((upper(col))). Translate the expression and mark custom functions IMMUTABLE only if they truly are.

### O2PG-PF-003: Reverse key indexes

severity **low** · effort 0.25

Reverse key indexes spread sequential keys across leaf blocks to reduce RAC contention. PostgreSQL has no reverse key option and no RAC block contention.

**Remediation:** Use a plain B-tree index. Range scans on the column start working again, which may change plans for the better.

### O2PG-PF-004: Index-organized tables

severity **medium** · effort 0.75

IOTs store rows in primary key order inside the index. PostgreSQL tables are heaps; CLUSTER reorders once but is not maintained.

**Remediation:** Create a heap table with the primary key. For small lookup tables that is all. For range-scanned IOTs, add INCLUDE columns to the primary key index to get index-only scans, and keep autovacuum healthy so the visibility map stays current.

### O2PG-PF-005: Domain indexes (Oracle Text and others)

severity **high** · effort 2

Domain indexes such as Oracle Text CONTEXT/CTXCAT have no equivalent, and the CONTAINS/CATSEARCH queries that use them must be rewritten.

**Remediation:** Use PostgreSQL full text search: a tsvector generated column with a GIN index and @@ to_tsquery(...). Check language configuration and ranking against the Oracle results. Spatial domain indexes: see the SDO_GEOMETRY rule.

### O2PG-PF-006: Foreign keys without a supporting index

severity **low** · effort 0.1

Neither database indexes foreign key columns automatically. Unindexed foreign keys make parent deletes and updates scan the child table, which hurts more under PostgreSQL's MVCC.

**Remediation:** Create an index whose leading columns are the foreign key columns.

### O2PG-PF-007: Compressed tables

severity **low** · effort 0.25

Basic, OLTP/advanced and hybrid columnar compression have no PostgreSQL equivalent; only large values are compressed (TOAST). Expect the data to grow on disk.

**Remediation:** Size Azure storage from uncompressed volumes, not Oracle segment sizes. Consider lz4 TOAST compression (default_toast_compression) for wide text columns.

### O2PG-PF-008: Very large tables

severity **medium** · effort 1

Tables with more than 50,000,000 rows according to optimizer statistics. Load time, index builds and validation for these drive the cutover window.

**Remediation:** Plan these separately: parallel load by key range or partition, create indexes after the load, and consider partitioning in PostgreSQL even if Oracle did not.

### O2PG-PF-009: Clustered tables

severity **medium** · effort 0.5

Index and hash clusters store rows of several tables together. PostgreSQL has no clusters in this sense.

**Remediation:** Create ordinary tables with the cluster key indexed on each.

## azure-specific

### O2PG-AZ-001: DBMS_SCHEDULER jobs that run SQL or PL/SQL

severity **medium** · effort 0.75 · extensions: `pg_cron`

Scheduled database work. pg_cron is supported on Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server and covers the common cases, with cron syntax instead of calendar expressions.

**Remediation:** Add pg_cron to shared_preload_libraries and azure.extensions (restart required), CREATE EXTENSION pg_cron in the database named by cron.database_name, then cron.schedule(...) or cron.schedule_in_database(...). Translate repeat_interval calendar strings to cron expressions; job chains and windows need app logic.

### O2PG-AZ-002: Scheduler jobs that run OS executables or scripts

severity **blocker** · effort 2

EXECUTABLE and script jobs run programs on the database host. A managed service gives you no host access.

**Remediation:** Move them to Azure Automation, Azure Functions with a timer trigger, Container Apps jobs or whatever scheduler the rest of your platform uses.

### O2PG-AZ-003: Advanced Queuing

severity **high** · effort 3

Oracle AQ queues and the code that enqueues or dequeues. PostgreSQL has no built-in message queue.

**Remediation:** For in-database work queues, a table plus SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and LISTEN/NOTIFY works well. For integration between systems, use Azure Service Bus and an outbox table written in the same transaction.

### O2PG-AZ-004: Database character set is not Unicode

severity **medium** · effort 2

Azure Flexible Server databases are normally created as UTF8. Data from a single-byte or legacy character set is converted on load, and invalid bytes that Oracle stored without complaint will be rejected.

**Remediation:** Scan for unconvertible data before the migration (Oracle DMU or a CSSCAN-style check), fix it at the source, and make sure the load tool declares the source encoding correctly. Re-check column lengths for characters that grow in UTF-8.

### O2PG-AZ-005: orafce could shorten the conversion

severity **info** · effort 0 · extensions: `orafce`

The code uses Oracle built-ins that the orafce extension implements. orafce is on the Flexible Server allow-list.

**Remediation:** Allow-list orafce in azure.extensions and CREATE EXTENSION orafce. Use it as a bridge to get code running, then decide whether to keep the dependency; plain PostgreSQL equivalents are easier for the next team to maintain.

### O2PG-AZ-006: Java stored procedures and external C procedures

severity **blocker** · effort 4

Java sources and call specs for Java or C routines. Azure Flexible Server does not support untrusted languages or loading your own shared libraries.

**Remediation:** Rewrite in PL/pgSQL if the logic is small, otherwise move it into an application service the database no longer calls directly.
